purpose: Single inexpensive motion prototype, not production-selected footage
prompt:
Five-second photorealistic live-action sci-fi advertising shot, one continuous locked-off wide shot. Use the supplied starting frame as the exact initial composition and as the authority for Riley's identity, gold dress, skin/chrome inlays, black-and-gold boots, facial cyberware, station and lighting. Riley has ALREADY upgraded when the clip begins. This is a calm confident reveal, not a transformation.

From the first frame she stands with her feet planted beside the closed train doors. She makes one small natural exhale, subtly relaxes her shoulders and lifts her chin just a fraction, maintaining a composed forward gaze. Her mouth stays closed. The movement is restrained and believable. Her bob shifts slightly in the station air; gold fabric catches the existing light with tiny natural movements. The cyan eye on viewer RIGHT stays softly illuminated without a flash, floating HUD or change of face. Hold her confident pose through the end, allowing clean edit handles.

Keep the camera completely fixed: no push-in, zoom, pan, tilt, reframing, shake or cuts. Keep her head size and position, body proportions, feet, five-finger hands, gold dress silhouette, natural skin and sparse chrome inlays consistent. Preserve the asymmetric facial hardware on viewer RIGHT and the mechanical neck. Do not mirror her, replace her arms or legs with metal, make her walk or run, or change her outfit. The train remains stationary with the doors closed. Preserve carriage 07, platform architecture, skyline, wet reflections, morning light, cyan/magenta accents and existing background geometry.

Audio: only a quiet steady distant station and train ventilation ambience. No speech, lip-sync, announcements, music, footsteps, voiceover or activation sound. No added text, captions, logos, new people, particles, morphs, energy bursts or transition effects. The instant upgrade cut and the original narration will be added separately during editing.
